Tropical rain forests have high rainfall and warm temperatures that promote rapid decomposition and nutrient cycling, but heavy rainfall also causes significant leaching of nutrients from the soil.  
Tundra has slow decomposition due to cold temperatures, so nutrients remain locked in organic matter.  
Taiga (boreal forest) also has slow decomposition and moderate leaching.  
Deserts have low rainfall, so leaching is minimal.  

Thus, tropical rain forest soils experience the highest rate of leaching and nutrient cycling.  

Final answer: (A)
